system.name: Syndicate
system.one_liner: a system that jointly optimizes ML collective communication scheduling and execution planning for distributed training

components.name: Model (PyTorch, etc.)
components.role: application-level model definition, the first step toward a comm-op

components.name: Parallelization Strategy (Data- / Model- / etc.)
components.role: determines how the model and data are parallelized across devices

components.name: Comm-Op Scheduler (DDP / ByteScheduler / etc.)
components.role: schedules the communication collectives that parallelization requires

components.name: Comm-Op Interface (ProcessGroup / etc.)
components.role: generic interface abstraction through which scheduled comm-ops are issued to the backend

components.name: Comm-Op Execution (NCCL / etc.)
components.role: executes the communication operation over the network

components.name: Worker Processes
components.role: the per-device processes across which this entire stack is replicated

content.key_idea: Existing ML training systems layer communication handling into an App Layer (model, parallelization strategy, comm-op scheduling) and a Comm Layer (a generic interface handing off to a backend like NCCL), with four numbered steps leading to a comm-op's network execution.
content.reading_order: Top-down through four numbered stages: Model, Parallelization Strategy, and Comm-Op Scheduler in the App Layer, then Comm-Op Interface and Comm-Op Execution in the Comm Layer, replicated per Worker Process; side diagrams illustrate the tensor operator graph, training DAG, schedule order, and per-device execution.

palette.used_for: light yellow/cream fill for the main stage boxes
bright yellow accent, e.g. layer-label backgrounds
amber/gold accent, e.g. circled step-number fill
light gray background shading for the outer Worker Processes box
amber accent shared with the gold tones above

style.stroke: solid black borders (~1.2pt) on stage boxes, dashed lines separating the stack from the side illustrative diagrams
style.font: Times New Roman serif, about 5-8pt body text with an 11pt title (Existing System Stack), mostly not bold
style.arrows: downward arrows with filled heads linking the four numbered stages, plus curved arrows in the small side diagrams

encoding.color_means: yellow/gold fill uniformly marks the existing-system stack boxes with no further semantic color coding
encoding.emphasis: circled numbers 1-4 directly on the stack trace the exact sequence a comm-op follows from model definition down to network execution
reusable_patterns: layered app-layer/comm-layer stack with numbered steps
side-by-side abstract diagrams (tensor operator graph, training DAG, schedule order, execution) illustrating each stage's output
weaknesses: App Layer / Comm Layer bracket labels sit visually apart from the boxes they group
side diagrams use dense mathematical notation (op3(op2(x),op1(x))) that requires careful reading

summary: This figure, titled 'Existing System Stack,' lays out the baseline ML-training communication stack that motivates SYNDICATE's design (contrasted later with SYNDICATE's own stack in Figure 7). It shows two layers: an App Layer containing Model (PyTorch, etc.), Parallelization Strategy (Data-/Model-parallel, etc.), and Comm-Op Scheduler (DDP/ByteScheduler, etc.); and a Comm Layer containing Comm-Op Interface (ProcessGroup, etc.) and Comm-Op Execution (NCCL, etc.), all replicated per Worker Process. Four circled numbers trace the steps from model definition down to a comm-op's network execution. Side diagrams illustrate each stage's abstraction: a tensor operator graph for the model's forward pass, a training DAG assigning forward/backward ops across devices a/b/c, a scheduled device order, and per-device execution streams performing an all-reduce via NCCL ring all-reduce. The figure uses flat yellow/gold-filled boxes with black borders and serif text, without color-coding beyond a uniform stage fill.
summary_zh: 该图为'现有系统栈'，展示ML训练通信栈的应用层（模型、并行策略、通信调度器）与通信层（ProcessGroup接口、NCCL执行），四个编号步骤对应SYNDICATE的对比基线（见图7）。
notes: This figure is explicitly the 'Existing System Stack' (a generic/baseline architecture used for motivation), not SYNDICATE's own design; the paper's proposed stack is shown separately in Figure 7. All components here are marked non-novel accordingly.
